title: The Output Convergence Debate Revisited: Lessons from recent developments in the analysis of panel data models - Replication Spec
hypothesis: Under heterogeneous dynamics and nonparallel trends (trended latent technology factor) TWFE and Barro estimates of speed of convergence phi=1-rho are biased toward zero; DCCE estimators consistent. Empirically cross-country unconditional convergence very slow (Barro phi 0.3-0.6% mean lag 171-315y), within-country to country-specific trends reasonably fast (TWFE ~3% ~25y, DCCEMG ~11% ~6y business-cycle frequency). Capital long-run elasticity ~0.48 near 0.46 capital share; TI conflict and property rights significant; democracy positive but significance falls after allowing nonparallel trends/heterogeneity.
data_sources: PWT 10.01 rgdpna, rgdpo, rnna, pop, emp 1950-2019
Acemoglu Naidu Restrepo Robinson 2019 replication dataset 1960-2010 dichotomous democracy
Kremer Willis You 2022 TI covariates: absolute latitude, ethnic fractionalization, protection against expropriation risk
sample: Penn World Tables PWT 10.01 rgdpna (real GDP at constant 2017 national prices, million 2017US$) /POP and /EMP: y_it=log(Y_it/POP_it) per capita and tilde y_it=log(Y_it/EMP_it) per employee 1950-2019 baseline unbalanced panel 157 countries with >=30 obs (effective >=26 after 4 lags, Tmin 27/26, Tave 55.2/54.2 per capita 52/51 per employee, Tmax 67/66). Barro cross-section balanced 157 countries 1990-2019 dependent y_{i,2019}-y_{i,1990} on y_{i,1990} and PPP adjustment y_{i,1990}-y_{i,1990}^{PPP} (rgdpo). Capital panel ARDL(2,2) same 157 countries k_it=log(K_it/POP_it) rnna. Democracy replication Acemoglu et al. 2019 1960-2010 n=175 -> filtered n=148 with >=24 raw (>=20 after lags, Tmin 20, Tave 40, Tmax 47) dichotomous democracy d_it 0/1; 75 invariant, 73 varying; DCCEMG full heterogeneity n=73 treated. Time-invariant second stage cross-country n=100 of hat a_i = bar y_i - bar q_i' psi_hat (psi_hat TWFE/DCCEP ARDL(2,2)) on z_i: absolute latitude, ethnolinguistic fractionalization, protection from expropriation, PPP gap y_{1990}-y^{PPP}_{1990} (Kremer et al. 2022, divided by 100). Summary descriptives also report latitude n=144, ELF 121, protection 107.
method: Step 1: Construct y_it=log(rgdpna/POP_it) and tilde y_it=log(rgdpna/EMP_it) and k_it=log(rnna/POP_it), tilde k_it=log(rnna/EMP_it) from PWT 10.01 1950-2019; keep countries with >=30 time observations; use unbalanced panels; compute cross-section averages bar y_{.t}=n_t^{-1} sum_i y_it and bar k_{.t} and bar d_{.t} for democracy (using n=148 sample averages for DCCEMG n=73); global output GLO = PPP-weighted 1/3 each Asia Europe North America simple average for illustration mean growth 2.4% p.a.

Step 2: Barro cross-country OLS (heteroskedasticity-robust): estimate (3) y_{i,2019}-y_{i,1990}=a_T+b_T y_{i,1990}+c_T(y_{i,1990}-y^{PPP}_{i,1990})+zeta_{iT} on balanced n=157 T=29 (1990-2019); recover phi=1-(1+b_T)^{1/T} and mean lag=(1-phi)/phi; test restriction c_T=-b_T (t=-3.10 per capita, -3.96 per employee). Also estimate restricted models c_T=0 (cols 2).

Step 3: Panel AR(3) no covariates: Dynamic model (9) Delta y_it = alpha_i + gamma_i f_t - phi y_{i,t-1}+ psi1 Delta y_{i,t-1}+ psi2 Delta y_{i,t-2}+u_it. Estimate three ways: (i) TWFE two-way fixed effects (parallel trends homogeneous phi) via within transformation (xtreg); (ii) DCCEP pooled dynamic CCE (6) y_it = (alpha_i-delta_i0 bar alpha)+ delta_i0 bar y_{.t}+delta_i1 bar y_{.t-1}+ rho y_{i,t-1}+... proxied by Hbar=(tau_T, bar y, bar y_{-1},...,bar y_{-3}) using generalized inverse Mbar=I - Hbar(Hbar'Hbar)^- Hbar' (Stata xtdcce2 Ditzen 2021, p=3 q=3); (iii) DCCEMG mean-group (11) estimate country-specific phi_i via Delta y_it = alpha_i -phi_i y_{i,t-1}+... + psi_i0 bar y_{.t}+ sum_{s=0}^{3} psi_is Delta bar y_{.t-s}+u_it with q=4 p=3, then phi_DCCEMG=n^{-1} sum_i phi_i_hat and Var=n^{-1}(n-1)^{-1} sum_i (phi_i_hat - phi_DCCEMG)^2. Report phi=-coef(y_{t-1}), psi1, psi2, mean lag=(1-phi-psi1-psi2)/phi. Unbalanced, robust SE Huber-White for TWFE, heteroskedasticity-robust for DCCE. Same for tilde y_it.

Step 4: Panel with capital ARDL(2,2): (12) Delta y_it = alpha_i -phi_i y_{i,t-1}+ sum delta Delta y + beta_i' x_it + sum lambda Delta x + psi' bar w + u_it where x=k (per capita matching per capita, per employee matching) and bar w=(bar y, bar k). DCCEP augments with {bar y_t,bar k_t, bar y_{t-1},bar k_{t-1}, bar y_{t-2},bar k_{t-2}, bar y_{t-3},bar k_{t-3}}; DCCEMG adds bar y_{t-4},bar k_{t-4}. Estimate TWFE/DCCEP/DCCEMG as before, report impact phi, k_{t-1}, Delta k, Delta k_{t-1}, Delta k_{t-2} and long-run beta_LR = -beta/phi with delta-method SE.

Step 5: Democracy replication: Use Acemoglu et al. (2019) replication dataset y_it=log output per capita, d_it dichotomous democracy 1960-2010. Estimate (i) TWFE full n=175 and filtered n=148 (drop T_i<24 raw), (ii) DCCEP n=148 homogeneous democracy coefficient with cross-section averages {bar y_t,...,bar y_{t-4}, bar d_t}, (iii) DCCEMG* n=148 homogeneous democracy but heterogeneous dynamics, (iv) DCCEMG n=73 fully heterogeneous (only varying d). Four lags of output (error correction with 3 Delta lags). Long-run = coef(d)/phi. Robustness check dropping bar d_t (coefficient falls 0.947 t1.65 ->0.748 t1.27).

Step 6: Time-invariant covariates: After Step 4 ARDL(2,2) obtain psi_hat = TWFE or DCCEP (pooled). For n=100 with TI data compute filtered average a_i_T = bar y_i - bar q_i' psi_hat where bar q_i includes lagged output and capital means. Then cross-country OLS (8) a_i = alpha_T + theta' z_i + eta_iT + bar u_i with z=(absolute latitude, ELF, protection from expropriation, PPP gap), all z divided by 100. Report OLS coefficients with heteroskedasticity-robust SE; Tmax 68, Tmin 48 pc /38 pe, Tave 63 pc /61 pe.
